row.title: The Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for books
row.statement:
Let $B_m$ be the book with $m$ pages, defined by

$$
B_m=K_2+\overline{K_m}.
$$

For a graph $H$, let $R(H,H)$ denote its two-color Ramsey number, and let $gr_k(K_3:B_m)$ be the minimum order of a complete graph whose every $k$-coloring contains either a rainbow $K_3$ or a monochromatic $B_m$.

**Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for books.** For $k\geq 2$,

$$
gr_k(K_3:B_m)=\begin{cases}(R(B_m,B_m)-1)\cdot5^{(k-2)/2}+1 & \text{if $k$ is even,}\\2\cdot(R(B_m,B_m)-1)\cdot5^{(k-3)/2}+1 & \text{if $k$ is odd.}\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture asserts that the lower bounds obtained in the paper are sharp, giving exact Gallai-Ramsey numbers for books. The surrounding conclusion presents only bounds and says that the conjecture is being offered because the authors believe the lower bound to be sharp; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
row.source_name: Jinyu Zou, Yaping Mao, Colton Magnant, Zhao Wang and Chengfu Ye, “Gallai-Ramsey numbers for books”, arXiv:1802.04930 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04930

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

row.title: Matsuda–Ozeki–Yamashita's branch-vertex conjecture for claw-free graphs
row.statement:
Let $k$ be a non-negative integer and let $G$ be a connected claw-free graph of order $n$. For an integer $r\geq 2$, let $\sigma_r(G)$ be the minimum degree sum of an independent set of $r$ vertices in $G$:

$$
\sigma_r(G)=\min\left\{\sum_{x\in S}\deg_G(x): S\subseteq V(G),\ |S|=r,\ S\text{ is independent}\right\}.
$$

A vertex of degree at least three in a tree is called a branch vertex. **Matsuda–Ozeki–Yamashita's conjecture.** Let $k$ be a non-negative integer and let $G$ be a connected claw-free graph of order $n$. If

$$
\sigma_{2k+3}(G)\geq n-2,
$$

then $G$ has a spanning tree with at most $k$ branch vertices.
This conjecture proposes a sharper degree-sum condition for spanning trees with boundedly many branch vertices in connected claw-free graphs, improving on earlier sufficient conditions. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
row.source_name: Pham Hoang Ha and Dang Dinh Hanh, “Spanning trees with at most 2 branch vertices in claw - free graphs”, arXiv:1806.00734 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.00734

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

row.title: Composite-degree extremal reciprocal polynomial conjecture
row.statement:
Let $\mathrm{mr}(d)$ be the minimum of the houses of reciprocal algebraic integers of degree $d$ that are not roots of unity, and let $R_d(x)$ be the minimal polynomial of an extremal reciprocal algebraic integer. Let $d$ be composite, and let $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ be odd prime divisors of $d$ or elements of $\{s,t\}$, where $s=9$ and

$$
t=1;\qquad t=4\text{ if }8\mid d\text{ and }12\nmid d;\qquad t=6\text{ if }12\mid d.
$$

Suppose

$$
\mathrm{mr}^{2p_1}(2p_1)<\mathrm{mr}^{2p_2}(2p_2)<\cdots<\mathrm{mr}^{2p_k}(2p_k).
$$

**Composite-degree extremal reciprocal polynomial conjecture.** If $R_{2p_i}(x)$ is the minimal polynomial of the extremal reciprocal algebraic integer of degree $2p_i$, then

$$
R_d(x)=R_{2p_1}(x^{d/(2p_1)})
$$

and

$$
\mathrm{mr}(d)=\lvert R_{2p_1}(x^{d/(2p_1)})\rvert.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the computed smallest houses of reciprocal polynomials and would reduce composite-degree reciprocal cases to selected lower-degree cases. No resolution status is given in the source.
row.source_name: Dragan Stankov, “The House of a Reciprocal Algebraic Integer”, arXiv:1806.06424 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.06424

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

row.title: The column-equivalence partition realization conjecture for permutations
row.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a partition of $\mathopen{[\![} 1,n\mathclose{]\!]}$, and let $\mathbb{F}$ be an infinite field. For a mapping $f:\mathfrak{S}_n\to\mathbb{F}^*$, define column-$f$-equivalence on $\mathopen{[\![} 1,n\mathclose{]\!]}$ by identifying the indices that determine the same column-equivalence class, and let its quotient set be the resulting partition. **Column-equivalence partition realization conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}$ does not have exactly two elements, one of which is a singleton, then there exists a mapping

$$
f: \mathfrak{S}_n \rightarrow \mathbb{F}^*
$$

such that $\mathcal{F}$ is the quotient set for column-$f$-equivalence. This conjecture asks which partitions can occur as column-equivalence partitions of mappings on the symmetric group; the source presents this realization problem as open over infinite fields.
row.source_name: Clément de Seguins Pazzis, “On the linear preservers of Schur matrix functionals”, arXiv:1807.06264 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06264

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2018).

row.title: Powered adjacency eigenvectors achieve weak recovery in the geometric block model
row.statement:
Let $\mathrm{GBM}(n,s,t)$ be the geometric block model, let $G$ be a graph from this model, let $d=\operatorname{diam}(G)$, and let $A^{(r)}$ denote the powered adjacency matrix. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, set $r=\varepsilon d$. Weak recovery is the task of recovering the communities with nontrivial accuracy.

**Powered adjacency conjecture.** Let $s,t\geq 0$ and suppose $\mathrm{GBM}(n,s,t)$ has a giant component. Taking the second-largest eigenvector of $A^{(r)}$, with $r=\varepsilon\cdot\operatorname{diam}(G)$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, and rounding it by signs or by the median solves weak recovery in $\mathrm{GBM}(n,s,t/\sqrt{n})$ whenever weak recovery is solvable.

The conjecture asserts that graph powering followed by a spectral partition reaches the efficient weak-recovery threshold in the geometric block model. No resolution is supplied in the source.
row.source_name: Emmanuel Abbe, Enric Boix, Peter Ralli and Colin Sandon, “Graph powering and spectral robustness”, arXiv:1809.04818 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04818

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

row.title: Quantum D-module conjecture for primitive extremal transitions
row.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth projective varieties related by a primitive extremal transition. Denote by $\mathcal{H}(X)$ the ambient part of the quantum $D$-module of $X$. After analytic continuation of $\mathcal{H}(X)$ over the extended Kähler moduli, write the resulting $D$-module as $\bar{\mathcal{H}}(X)$. Then there are a divisor $E$ and a submodule $\bar{\mathcal{H}}^E(X)\subseteq\bar{\mathcal{H}}(X)$ with maximum trivial $E$-monodromy such that

$$
\bar{\mathcal{H}}^E(X)|_E\simeq\mathcal{H}(Y),
$$

where $\bar{\mathcal{H}}^E(X)|_E$ denotes the restriction to $E$. This conjecture proposes a relationship between the ambient quantum $D$-modules of the two varieties across a primitive extremal transition, generalizing the proposed comparison for cubic extremal transitions; the statement concerns analytic continuation and restriction rather than equivalence of the full Gromov–Witten theories.
row.source_name: Rongxiao Mi, “Gromov-Witten theory under degree-4 Type II Extremal Transitions”, arXiv:1810.05783 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05783

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

row.title: Wang's Turán-number conjecture for spanning linear forests
row.statement:
Let $r$-linear forests be $r$-uniform hypergraphs consisting of vertex-disjoint tight paths or isolated vertices, and let $\mathcal{L}^r_{n,k}$ be the set of all $r$-linear forests of order $n$ with at least $k$ edges. For $k=mr+1$ with $m\geq 1$, write $ex_r(n;\mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{n,k})$ for the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no member of $\mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{n,k}$. **Wang's conjecture.** For $k=mr+1$ and $m\geq 1$, 

$$
ex_r(n;\mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{n,k})=\max\left\{\binom{k+r-2}{r},\binom{n}{r}-\binom{n-(k-1)/r}{r}\right\}.
$$

This conjecture extends the graph case and is motivated by tight linear forests as an intermediate concept between matchings and Hamilton tight cycles; it implies the Erdős Matching Conjecture. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
row.source_name: Bo Ning and Jian Wang, “The formula for Turán number of spanning linear forests”, arXiv:1812.01047 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.01047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

row.title: Extremal Khovanov homology signature conjecture for Turaev genus one links
row.statement:
Let $L$ be a non-split link of Turaev genus one. Write $Kh^{i,j}(L)$ for its Khovanov homology, let $j_{\min}(L)$ and $j_{\max}(L)$ denote the minimum and maximum quantum gradings supporting Khovanov homology, and let $\sigma(L)$ be its signature. **Signature conjecture.** At least one of the following statements holds:

1. There is an $i_0\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
 
$$
Kh^{*,j_{\min}(L)}(L)=Kh^{i_0(L),j_{\min}(L)}(L)\cong\mathbb{Z}
$$

 and
 
$$
2i_0(L)-j_{\min}(L)=\sigma(L)+1.
$$

2. There is an $i_0\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
 
$$
Kh^{*,j_{\max}(L)}(L)=Kh^{i_0(L),j_{\max}(L)}(L)\cong\mathbb{Z}
$$

 and
 
$$
2i_0(L)-j_{\max}(L)=\sigma(L)-1.
$$

This weakens the hypotheses of the preceding signature theorem, which assumes that the link has both an $A$-Turaev genus one and a $B$-Turaev genus one diagram. The conjecture is open for links that are $A$-Turaev genus one but not $B$-Turaev genus one, and vice versa.
row.source_name: Oliver T. Dasbach and Adam M. Lowrance, “Extremal Khovanov homology of Turaev genus one links”, arXiv:1812.11387 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.11387

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2018). “Conjecture is open for links that are $A$-Turaev genus one, but not $B$-Turaev genus one (and vice versa).”

row.title: The Gallai-Ramsey reduction conjecture for rainbow $P_{5}$
row.statement:
Let $P_{5}$ be the path on five vertices, let $H$ be a graph with no isolated vertices, and let $k$ be a positive integer. The Gallai-Ramsey number $gr_k(P_{5}:H)$ is the minimum integer $n$ such that every coloring of $K_n$ using at most $k$ colors contains either a rainbow copy of $P_{5}$ or a monochromatic copy of $H$. Let $R_3(H)$ denote the minimum integer $n$ such that every coloring of $K_n$ using at most three colors contains a monochromatic copy of $H$.

**Gallai-Ramsey reduction conjecture.** For any graph $H$ with no isolated vertices, we have

$$
gr_k(P_{5}:H)=R_3(H).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the Gallai-Ramsey problem for avoiding a rainbow $P_{5}$ reduces to the three-color Ramsey number. The paper provides several results in support of this claim, but no resolution is supplied here.
row.source_name: Xihe Li, Pierre Besse, Colton Magnant, Ligong Wang and Noah Watts, “Gallai-Ramsey numbers for rainbow paths”, arXiv:1902.00612 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.00612

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

row.title: Conjectured structure of quartic graphs with minimum spectral gap
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected quartic graph, meaning a connected $4$-regular graph, on $n\geq 11$ vertices. Let $M_1$ denote the specified middle block and $D_1,D_2,D_4,D_5$ the specified end blocks from the source. Choose non-negative integers $q$ and $r<5$ satisfying

$$
n-11=5q+r.
$$

A graph is formed by concatenating $q$ middle blocks and the indicated end blocks.

**Quartic minimum-gap conjecture.** The connected quartic graph on $n\geq 11$ vertices with minimum spectral gap is the unique graph $G$ described as follows: $G$ consists of $q$ middle blocks $M_1$, with end blocks chosen according to $r$. If $r=0$, both end blocks are $D_4$; if $r=1$, they are $D_4$ and $D_1$; if $r=2$, both are $D_1$; if $r=3$, they are $D_1$ and $D_2$; and if $r=4$, they are $D_4$ and $D_5$.

This conjecture seeks the precise extremal structure, beyond the paper's theorem describing the general path-like block structure of quartic graphs with minimum spectral gap. The block definitions are supplied by figures elsewhere in the paper, and the assertion is not marked as resolved in the provided text.
row.source_name: M. Abdi, E. Ghorbani and W. Imrich, “Regular Graphs with Minimum Spectral Gap”, arXiv:1907.03733 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.03733

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

row.title: The extremal-function classification conjecture for binary (3, t)-formations
row.statement:
Let $t\geq 6$. A **$(3,t)$-formation** is a concatenation of $t$ permutations of three distinct letters. Consider formations $u$ whose first permutation is $a b c$ and whose remaining permutations are each either $a b c$ or $a c b$. The **formation-width** $\operatorname{fw}(u)$ is the least integer $s$ such that every binary $(3,s)$-formation contains $u$ as a subsequence.

**Extremal-function classification conjecture.** Among these formations, $\operatorname{fw}(u)=2t-1$ if and only if $u$ is one of

$$
(a b c)^{t},\quad a b c (a c b)^{t-1},\quad a b c (a c b)^{t-2} a b c,\quad a b c a c b (a b c)^{t-3} a c b,
$$

$$
a b c a c b (a b c)^{t-2},\quad a b c a b c (a c b)^{t-2},\quad (a b c)^{t-2} a c b a c b,\quad (a b c)^{t-2} a c b a b c,\quad (a b c)^{t-1} a c b.
$$

This conjecture proposes a complete classification of the formations attaining the extremal value $2t-1$, extending the evidence and preceding proposition in the paper; its resolution would determine precisely which binary $(3,t)$-formations have maximal formation-width in this setting.
row.source_name: Jesse Geneson, “An algorithm for bounding extremal functions of forbidden sequences”, arXiv:1912.04897 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04897

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

row.title: Hou–Jagadeesan maximal partition-rank product conjecture modulo 2
row.statement:
For a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k)$, define

$$
N(r,t;\lambda):=\prod_{j=1}^{k}N(r,t;\lambda_j).
$$

Let $P(n)$ be the set of partitions of $n$, and define

$$
\operatorname{maxN}(r,t;n):=\max\bigl\{N(r,t;\lambda):\lambda\in P(n)\bigr\}.
$$

**Hou–Jagadeesan's maximal-value conjecture.** The following are true:

1. If $n\geq 5$, then

$$
\operatorname{maxN}(0,2;n)=
\begin{cases}
3^{n/3} & n\equiv 0\pmod{3},\\
11\cdot 3^{(n-7)/3} & n\equiv 1\pmod{3},\\
5\cdot 3^{(n-5)/3} & n\equiv 2\pmod{3},
\end{cases}
$$

and the maximum is attained at the unique partitions $(3,3,\ldots,3)$, $(3,3,\ldots,7)$, and $(3,3,\ldots,5)$ in the respective congruence classes modulo $3$. If $n\geq 8$, then

$$
\operatorname{maxN}(1,2;n)=
\begin{cases}
2^{n/2} & n\equiv 0\pmod{2},\\
12\cdot 2^{(n-9)/2} & n\equiv 1\pmod{2},
\end{cases}
$$

and the maximum is attained by $(2,2,\ldots,2)$ when $n$ is even and $(2,2,\ldots,9)$ when $n$ is odd, up to any number of substitutions $(2,2)\to(4)$ and $(2,2,2)\to(6)$. The source presents this as a conjecture of Hou and Jagadeesan, without supplying a resolution in the provided text.
row.source_name: Kevin Gomez and Eric Zhu, “Bounds for Coefficients of the f(q) Mock Theta Function and Applications to Partition Ranks”, arXiv:2008.08253 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08253

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

row.title: The subcontraction conjecture for facial 3-colorability and 3-flows
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A graph is **facially $3$-colorable** if it has a facial $3$-coloring, and **$3$-flowable** if it admits a nowhere-zero $3$-flow. For $n\geq 4$, let $K_{3,n}^+$ be the graph obtained from $K_{3,n}$ by joining two vertices in its partite set of size $3$ by an edge; a **subcontraction** is the graph operation used in the paper's definition.

**The subcontraction conjecture.** If $G$ is a facially $3$-colorable graph which does not have a subcontraction isomorphic to $K_{3,n}^+$ for some $n\geq 4$, then $G$ is $3$-flowable.

A positive answer would establish facial $3$-colorability and $3$-flowability as equivalent for graphs excluding the displayed obstructions as subcontractions. The paper proves this equivalence for graphs of maximum degree at most $3$ and for $K_{3,3}$-minor-free graphs, but the general assertion remains open.
row.source_name: Christoph Hertrich, Felix Schröder and Raphael Steiner, “Coloring Drawings of Graphs”, arXiv:2008.09692 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09692

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

row.title: Frankl and Kupavskii's matching–cover conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
row.statement:
Let $n,s,k$ be positive integers with $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq ks+k-1$. Let $H$ be a $k$-graph on vertex set $[n]$, and let $\nu(H)$ and $\tau(H)$ denote its matching number and vertex-cover number. For $2\leq i\leq k-1$, define

$$
A^k_i(n,s):=\\{e\in\binom{[n]}{k}:|e\cap[(s+1)i-1]|\geq i\\}.
$$

Let $S=\\{s+1,\ldots,s+k\\}$ and define

$$
HM^k_{n,s}:=\\{e\in\binom{[n]}{k}:e\cap[s-1]\neq\emptyset\\}\cup\\{S\\}\cup\\{e\in\binom{[n]}{k}:s\in e,\\ e\cap S\neq\emptyset\\}.
$$

For a set $U\subseteq[n]$ of size $k(s+1)-1$, let $D^k_{n,s}(U):=\\{e\in\binom{[n]}{k}:e\subseteq U\\}$, and write $D^k_{n,s}$ for this construction. **Frankl and Kupavskii's conjecture.** If $\nu(H)=s$ and $\tau(H)>s$, then

$$
e(H)\leq\max\\{|A^k_2(n,s)|,\ldots,|A^k_{k-1}(n,s)|,|HM^k_{n,s}|,|D^k_{n,s}|\\}.
$$

The listed constructions have matching number $s$ and vertex-cover number greater than $s$, so the conjecture proposes that they determine the maximum edge count among such hypergraphs. Its status is not resolved by the supplied text.
row.source_name: Mingyang Guo, Hongliang Lu and Dingjia Mao, “A stability result on matchings in 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2103.15127 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.15127

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

row.title: Hardness conjecture from zeros of the complex-valued Ising partition function
row.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be an integer with $\Delta \ge 3$ and let $\beta\in \mathbb{C}_{\mathbb{A}}$ with $\beta \not \in \mathbb{R}\cup \{i, -i\}$. Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, and let $Z_{\mathrm{Ising}}(G; \beta)$ denote its Ising partition function. The approximation problems $\textsc{IsingNorm}(\beta, \Delta, 1.01)$ and $\textsc{IsingArg}(\beta, \Delta, \pi/3)$ concern, respectively, approximating the norm and argument of this partition function. **Hardness conjecture from zeros.** If there is a graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ such that

$$
Z_{\mathrm{Ising}}(G; \beta) = 0,
$$

then the problems

$$
\textsc{IsingNorm}(\beta, \Delta, 1.01) \quad\text{and}\quad \textsc{IsingArg}(\beta, \Delta, \pi/3)
$$

are $\mathrm{\#P}$-hard. The surrounding discussion explains that a zero of the partition function can typically be used to implement the edge interaction $-1$, which yields hardness through the preceding lemma; the conjecture concerns the case where terminal-degree conditions are not established.
row.source_name: Andreas Galanis, Leslie Ann Goldberg and Andrés Herrera-Poyatos, “The complexity of approximating the complex-valued Ising model on bounded degree graphs”, arXiv:2105.00287 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.00287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

row.title: The dimension formula for the largest matchable subspace
row.statement:
Let $K\subset F$ be a field extension, and let $A$ and $B$ be two $n$-dimensional $K$-subspaces of $F$, where $n\geq 1$. Write $\langle AB\rangle$ for the $K$-linear span of the products of elements of $A$ and $B$, and let $M(A,B)$ denote the dimension of the largest subspace of $A$ that is matched to a subspace of $B$. For a basis $\mathcal{A}=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}$ of $A$, define

$$
D_{\mathcal{A}}(B)=\max\left\{\#J:J\subset\{1,\ldots,n\},\ \dim\bigcap_{i\in J}\left(a_i^{-1}A\cap B\right)>n-\#J\right\},
$$

and define

$$
D(A,B)=\max\{D_{\mathcal{A}}(B):\mathcal{A}\text{ is a basis for }A\}.
$$

**The dimension formula for the largest matchable subspace.** If $\langle AB\rangle\neq A$ and $A$ is not matched to $B$, then

$$
M(A,B)=n-D(A,B).
$$

This is the proposed linear analogue of the corresponding result for unmatchable subsets in groups. It relates the failure of the matching condition to the dimension of the largest subspace of $A$ that can still be matched to a subspace of $B$; the supplied text does not establish the formula or provide evidence resolving it.
row.source_name: Mohsen Aliabadi, Jack Kinseth, Christopher Kunz, Haris Serdarevic and Cole Wills, “Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions”, arXiv:2107.09029 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09029

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

row.title: Subgraph criterion for minimal doubled 3-regular graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a doubled 3-regular graph. Perform the YY-$\Delta$ transformation on all wyes in all possible ways to obtain a graph $G'$ of smallest size. A **chain of 3-cycles** is a chain of one or more 3-cycles, each connected by a vertex that is also doubly adjacent to one more vertex, with the 3-cycles at either end having one vertex with exactly 4 neighbours and no connections of size greater than 2.

**Minimality criterion conjecture.** The graph $G'$ is a minimal graph if and only if it does not contain such a chain of 3-cycles.

The conjecture proposes that, for doubled 3-regular graphs, checking the more restricted subgraphs illustrated in the first column of the paper's figure suffices to determine minimality. The source gives examples and discusses related reducible subgraphs, but provides no proof or resolution.
row.source_name: Shannon Jeffries and Karen Yeats, “A degree preserving delta wye transformation with applications to 6-regular graphs and Feynman periods”, arXiv:2110.07764 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07764

row.title: Conjectured exact minimum distances for D-sequence cyclic codes
row.statement:
Let $m=2^l e>2$, where $2\nmid e$ and $l\geq1$, and let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{D},i}$ denote the cyclic code associated with the sequence family $\mathcal{D}$. Let $h$ be the parameter used in the paper's definition of these codes, and let $d(\mathcal{C})$ denote minimum distance. **The D-sequence code minimum-distance conjecture.** If $l\geq2$ and $e>1$, then

$$
d(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{D},1})=2^{\frac{m}{2}}+4
$$

for even $h$, while

$$
d(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{D},1})=2^{\frac{m}{2}}+2
$$

for odd $h$. If $l=1$, then

$$
d(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{D},0})=2^{\frac{m}{2}}+2
$$

for $h=1$, and

$$
d(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{D},0})=2^{\frac{m}{2}}
$$

for $h=2$. The asserted values are further numerical predictions for the exact minimum distances of these cyclic codes; the supplied excerpt gives no resolution beyond the conjectural status.
row.source_name: Xianhong Xie, Yaxin Zhao, Zhonghua Sun and Xiaobo Zhou, “Binary [n,(n1)/2] cyclic codes with good minimum distances from sequences”, arXiv:2408.01906 (2024).
row.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2005.13623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.13623).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01906

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

row.title: Maximum independent edge set conjecture for 3-token graphs of paths
row.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\Gamma_3(P_n)$ denote its $3$-token graph. Write $\alpha'(G)$ for the maximum size of an independent edge set in a graph $G$. For any $n\geq 3$, the $3$-token graph $\Gamma_3(P_n)$ satisfies

**Maximum independent edge set conjecture.**

$$
\alpha'(\Gamma_3(P_n)) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\frac{n}{2}-1} \left(\sum_{i=1}^{2k-1} i \right)+ \sum_{i=1}^{\frac{n}{2}-1} i, & \text{if } n \text{ is even},\\[6pt] \displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\frac{n-1}{2}-1} \left(\sum_{i=1}^{2k} i \right)+ \sum_{i=1}^{\frac{n-1}{2}-1} i, & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}, \end{cases}
$$

and equivalently

$$
\alpha'(\Gamma_3(P_n)) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle \frac{n^3-3n^2+2n}{12}, & \text{if } n \text{ is even},\\[6pt] \displaystyle \frac{n^3-3n^2-n+3}{12}, & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}. \end{cases}
$$

The conjecture asserts that the displayed independent edge sets are maximum. The proposed formulas are based on explicit constructions for even and odd $n$; determining whether these constructions are largest remains an open problem for the $3$-token graphs of path graphs.
row.source_name: Felicia Servina Djuang, Arizka Yuliana, Widi Bagaskara and Yeni Susanti, “Exploring the 3-Token Graph of Particular Graphs”, arXiv:2511.10875 (2025).
row.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2107.00295](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00295).

row.title: Conlon–Lee subdivision extremal-number conjecture
row.statement: Let $k\ge 2$ be an even integer and let $H$ be a graph. Then there exists some $\delta>0$ such that $\operatorname{ex}(n,H^{k-1})=O\!\left(n^{1+1/k-\delta}\right)$, where $H^{k-1}$ is the $(k-1)$-subdivision of $H$.
